Description: There are many tourist attractions in and around Aberdeen. The new Municipal Water Park, the Dacotah Prairie Museum, Wylie Park, Thunder Road Amusement Park and Storybook Land are featured attractions just minutes from the Ramada Aberdeen Hotel. Other sights and attractions near the Ramada Aberdeen Hotel are Sand Lake National Wildlife Refuge, Richmond Lake and Mina Lake Recreation Areas and Hutterite Colony. Our Hotel is also close to Lee Park Golf Course and the Barnett Sports Complex. As a guest of Ramada you will enjoy our Free full hot breakfast -free for 2 people per room, a newly remodeled hotel with high speed internet access, large indoor heated pool and hot tub. New for 2009 is our poolside Tiki Bar and a new innovative bar called TapZ, where you can serve yourself cold tap beer right from your table. Bully''s Chop House featuring Steaks, Chops, Pasta and Seafood is now open. All of our hotels non-smoking guest rooms have the amenities you would expect such as 27 inch TV''s (many now have new 32 inch Flat screens) with expanded cable and HBO, Coffee Makers, Hair Dryers, many of our rooms have refrigerators and microwaves. Our spacious and flexible Convention Center, breaks down into eight separate rooms to hold meetings and banquets. Our pool side reception area is great for exhibit space, luncheons and social events. Pets allowed with one time fee of 25.00 per stay. Pets must be in a carrier. The Ramada Convention Center is conveniently located on Highway 12 making it quick and easy to get to your destination in Aberdeen. Our Ramada is just 5 minutes from Aberdeen Airport, LakeWood Mall and our downtown district. The Ramada is perfect for your every lodging need. Aberdeen is the home of the Northern State University Wolves and the Presentation College Saints. Both colleges are within a few miles of our hotel. There are many tourist attractions in and around Aberdeen.

Description:
Situated in the middle of all the action and adventure the Black Hills have to offer, the quaint Town Hall Inn has had many different incarnations over the years. Originally constructed as Leads town hall in 1912, the ornate building held many functions, including the mayors and treasurers office, court room, jail, judges chambers and even gallows, which were directly behind the building. On top of that, the Homestake Mining Company housed their general offices in the building for nearly 50 years.

The twelve rooms, with names such as Prosecution, Mayors Office and Auditors Office, each contain a flat screen TV, a microwave, a small refrigerator and an en suite bathroom. Theres also an array of lovely antique stores, eateries, museums, art galleries and the Historic Homestake Opera House all located on Leads Maine Street. Description:
Situated in the middle of all the action and adventure the Black Hills have to offer, the quaint Town Hall Inn has had many different incarnations over the years. Originally constructed as Leads town hall in 1912, the ornate building held many functions, including the mayors and treasurers office, court room, jail, judges chambers and even gallows, which were directly behind the building. On top of that, the Homestake Mining Company housed their general offices in the building for nearly 50 years.

The twelve rooms, with names such as Prosecution, Mayors Office and Auditors Office, each contain a flat screen TV, a microwave, a small refrigerator and an en suite bathroom. Theres also an array of lovely antique stores, eateries, museums, art galleries and the Historic Homestake Opera House all located on Leads Maine Street.
